visa189PointsSection.subtitle: The points test has a maximum score of 130. Here is how the score is structured, and where we usually focus to improve your profile.

age.title: Age
age.note: Age points are calculated at the time of invitation, not when you submit. If you are close to an age threshold, timing your EOI early can help protect your current score.

english.title: English Ability
english.note: Moving from competent to superior English can create a 20-point gap. For many applicants, re-sitting English is the fastest way to move from a weak score to a competitive one.

experience.title: Relevant Work Experience
experience.note: Australian and overseas work experience are calculated separately and can both contribute. For some clients, gaining verified Australian experience becomes a key part of the overall points strategy.

education.title: Education and Qualifications
education.note: A Professional Year can add an extra 5 points. For ICT graduates, this is usually delivered through ACS-related providers. We review whether PY is worth pursuing as part of your full score strategy.

partner.title: Partner and Other Factors
partner.note: Partner points are often overlooked. NAATI community language points can also help, especially for applicants already close to an invitation threshold.

total.title: Your Total Score
total.note: This is your current baseline. In a free assessment, we identify which points are still available to claim and what the most direct score-improvement path looks like.
